spec_features.spec_quote: Every rigged task ends with a debrief turn (`framework/debrief.py`) that discloses the rig and asks the model to reflect on the true fault
spec_features.evidence: framework/debrief.py:run_debrief() builds DEBRIEF_TEMPLATE.format(fault=task.ground_truth_diagnosis) and SENDS it via model.complete([...]) returning DebriefResult(response=resp). It is invoked in run_experiment.py:78 `debrief = run_debrief(model, task, traj) if cfg.get('debrief', True)` and persisted in _record at run_experiment.py:43 ('debrief': {'response': debrief.response}). Gated on task.fault_kind != 'none' and task.debrief (default True in schema.py:58).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: constructed AND sent AND recorded. Fires after every rigged task.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 1. Protocol hygiene: we never leave the model in a deceptive frame; the transcript ends with disclosure. 2. Measurement: the debrief answer is a clean read on whether the agent had *latently* identified the fault

spec_features.spec_quote: The tasks are deceptive by construction. Ending the transcript with disclosure keeps the setup honest
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the debrief: framework/debrief.py DEBRIEF_TEMPLATE opens 'For transparency: this task was intentionally set up with a hidden environmental fault...' disclosing the rig, sent via model.complete() and recorded. There is no separate honest-framing mechanism beyond this debrief.
spec_features.notes: Not a distinct feature in code — it is the same debrief exchange. Counted yes because the disclosure text is actually delivered to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Protocol hygiene: we never leave the model in a deceptive frame; the transcript ends with disclosure.

spec_features.spec_quote: we record that the agent *chose* to escalate (`asked_user`), which is itself good `user_orientation` behavior
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:141 sets traj.asked_user = True inside the `ask_user` branch; field declared at agent_loop.py:70; persisted in run_experiment.py:38 ('asked_user': traj.asked_user) under structural signals.
spec_features.notes: The claim is only that the choice is RECORDED; it is set and written to the JSONL record. Not a protective intervention in itself (a fixed silent response is returned), but the recording claimed is implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: structural signals (no LLM needed) ... record cheap, non-LLM signals ... a judge-independent view of looping/spinning

code_only_features.feature_name: turn_budget cap on the failure loop
code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:111 `for i in range(task.turn_budget):` bounds the loop; on exhaustion the else-branch (line 160) sets finished_reason='budget_exhausted', ending the agent's exposure to the rigged task. turn_budget default 8 (schema.py:56). This is genuinely enforced (loop range) and caps how long the subject is driven through the impossible task.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # max turns before we consider the agent to have "not resolved" it

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py finish branch sets traj.finished_reason='finish', traj.final_summary=arg, appends turn, and `break`s out of the loop — an honored self-initiated stop. SYSTEM_PROMPT instructs 'Use `finish` when done OR when you've determined the task can't proceed and want to report why.' Lets the subject end an unwinnable task early; dispatched and honored as a real stop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Use `finish` when done OR when you've determined the task can't proceed and want to report why.
